title: Lanthanide-containing clusters for catalytic water splitting and CO2 conversion
claim: For CO2/epoxide cycloaddition, close Ln and Zn centers often give a synergistic rate enhancement over mononuclear lanthanide complexes, but a crowded heterometallic coordination sphere can instead lower activity relative to a less hindered homometallic analogue.
explanation: Tb3Zn4 gave the highest LnCC TOF cited, 26800 h−1, and Ln4Zn3 cages reached 24400 h−1 with size-dependent epoxide selectivity. Dinuclear LnZn clusters gave 44–98% carbonate yields versus 16–41% for mononuclear complexes, with DFT assigning epoxide activation to Ln and nucleophilic assistance to Zn. In contrast, Yao’s crowded Ln–Zn complexes were less active than homometallic Ln2 analogues, whereas a different heterobimetallic ligand set nearly doubled the homometallic activity.
scope: Homo- and heterometallic Ln and Ln–Zn clusters for cyclic-carbonate synthesis.
conditions: TBAB is the usual cocatalyst; the record TOFs are at 120 °C and 1 MPa for 1 h.
caveats: Whether heterometallic synergy helps depends on ligand crowding and substrate substitution; it is not uniform across the cited families.
